text:
Tony DeAngelo is the kind of defenseman who makes his teammates' stat lines better and his coach nervous, and this season has been more of the first than usual. Stefen Rosner noted a strong night against the Devils: the shot that Victor Eklund tipped home, the stretch pass that started Anthony Duclair's goal, and solid work in his own end.

Our numbers flag him as due. The Islanders have scored 5.3 fewer goals than the chances deserve with him on the ice, which is why he has only five points in 16 games. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows he's a real setup man, 91st percentile among defensemen in primary shot assists, so the assists should start to come.

The cost is defensive. Evolving-Hockey had opponents creating more against him last season than against all but 1% of defensemen, and the tracking shows only 29% of his exits keep possession. With Ryan Pulock out, he's playing nearly 18 minutes a night. Our range has him at 24 to 41 points over a full season. Expect more points; keep an eye on the other end.
headline: DeAngelo's points should come
